checks.note: Mailbox API uses OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code and Client Credentials), Bearer header, 2-day (172800s) tokens, refresh tokens for Auth Code only, apps under Your Profile > My apps. Docs API separately uses an API key over HTTP Basic, so API key and Basic should also be listed.
Free plan has no API; Standard 200/min without reporting, Plus 400, Pro 800 with reporting. Page dated Jan 2025. The 15-day trial is not on the fetched page and stays unconfirmed.

Broad resource coverage (conversations, customers, inboxes, orgs, users, tags, teams, webhooks, workflows, reports). The page does not use the word REST, but it is HTTPS/JSON resource-based. Rate-limit page confirms account-wide limits and that writes and v3 searches count double.

Help Scout's own support article describes an official MCP at https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp. It is read-only for new connections, uses OAuth sign-in, and needs Standard or higher (reports need Plus or Pro).
ready_with_caveats is consistent: paid plan required, no reporting on Standard, shared account-wide limits with double-counted writes and searches, MCP read-only.

corrected.one_liner: Help Scout is a shared-inbox customer support platform with email, chat, a knowledge base (Docs) and reporting.
corrected.auth_notes: Mailbox API 2.0 uses OAuth 2.0 only. Authorization Code is for third-party integrations other users authorize. Client Credentials is for internal integrations. Apps are created under Your Profile > My apps. Tokens are sent as Bearer headers and expire after 2 days (172800s). Authorization Code also issues refresh tokens. The separate Docs API uses an API key sent over HTTP Basic (key as username, dummy password).
corrected.access_notes: The Free plan has no API access. Standard is the cheapest paid tier, with up to 200 calls/min and all endpoints except reporting. Plus allows 400 calls/min and Pro 800, and both include reporting. The limits table comes from a docs page last updated Jan 2025. A 15-day no-card trial was seen only in a search snippet and is unconfirmed. Prices were not checked.
corrected.blocker: The API needs a paid plan (Standard or higher), and Standard has no reporting endpoints. Rate limits are shared account-wide, and writes and v3 searches count double. The official MCP server is read-only for new connections, and its Docs tools need a separate Docs API key.
